findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) and String for status instead of typed enums/typestates. This allows illegal states such as is_sent: true with sent_at_epoch_ms: None, or status set to an arbitrary string not matching the domain lifecycle.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct or mutate PacketWorkflow into states that violate domain invariants. A packet could be marked sent without a timestamp, or have contradictory status/flag combinations. Any consumer must re-check invariants at every access point.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed PacketStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent). Replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a typestate pattern or derive them from PacketStatus. Make sent_at_epoch_ms a SentTimestamp(u64) newtype that is always present once status transitions to Sent.

findings.problem: id: String is a bare String with no domain typing. There is no PacketId newtype enforcing format, length, or uniqueness rules at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: Any string, including empty or malformed, is accepted as a packet ID. Validation must be repeated at every use site rather than guaranteed by construction.
findings.fix: Introduce pub struct PacketId(String) with a fallible constructor fn new(s: String) -> Result<PacketId, ParseError> that validates format and length. Use PacketId throughout.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and mutates a PacketWorkflow in place (item.status assignment), then returns the same type. This is mutation, not a pure functional transformation, and it discards typestate information.
findings.failure_mode: The function silently overwrites status and flags without enforcing a valid transition. It accepts a packet that may not be in a validated state and produces an inconsistent result. The return type is the same as the input, so callers cannot distinguish pre- and post-transition states.
findings.fix: Replace with a pure method or free function that takes a typed state (e.g., ValidatedPacket) and returns a new type (e.g., SentPacket) with the timestamp baked in. Use enum-based transitions so invalid state changes are a compile error.

findings.problem: No parse boundary exists. Raw String and bool values enter the struct with zero validation. The mark_sent function uses .to_string() on a hardcoded string literal instead of constructing from a validated domain value.
findings.failure_mode: External callers can pass arbitrary strings for id and status, bypassing any domain rules. There is no typed error type for invalid input, and no fallible constructor.
findings.fix: Add a PacketWorkflow::try_new(id: PacketId, initial_status: PacketStatus) -> Result<Self, ParseError> constructor. Reject all input at the boundary into typed domain values.

findings.problem: No domain error type exists. mark_sent returns PacketWorkflow with no way to signal that a transition was invalid (e.g., marking an already-sent packet, or marking an unvalidated packet as sent).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state transitions are silently accepted. Callers have no way to distinguish success from no-op. Error handling is absent.
findings.fix: Define pub enum PacketError { AlreadySent, NotValidated } and make mark_sent return Result<SentPacket, PacketError>.

residual_risk: The crate represents a primitive, untyped data carrier with mutation-based transitions. All domain invariants are expressed as runtime comments rather than compiler-enforced types. Without the typestate/enum refactoring, any consumer of this crate must independently enforce invariants, creating high risk of silent state corruption. Static review only; no commands run.
